attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own essay. It is not quoted from anyone else.

semantics.note: 'Explains' is slightly stronger than 'can be understood in this way', but in context Marcus attributes the errors to missing world models. The causal kind fits. No hedge applies.

contract.note: Asking for intervention studies across categories is a demanding test for an explanatory claim, but it is a reasonable way to check a causal attribution. The interpretive choices do not change the result: either way, the evidence does not settle it.

evidence.note: Links incoherent learned maps to detour failures in narrow navigation tasks. It does not cover the cited error categories (fake citations, images, video) or measure how many errors the mechanism explains.
A company disclosure showing that a misfiring answer-or-refuse circuit causes some hallucinations. This is a possible alternative mechanism, but it does not rule out world-model defects.

reviews.rationale: No study in the packet isolates world-model defects as the cause of errors across the cited categories, or measures the share of errors they explain. e6 is narrow supporting context. e7 offers another mechanism for some hallucinations without excluding Marcus's. The packet does not settle the causal claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own parenthetical in his own essay.

semantics.note: 'Might' qualifies only the concession that o3 may do better. 'Still vulnerable' is an unhedged present-tense observation. Adding 'of lacking world models' reflects the essay's theme but goes slightly past the words; the contract uses a behavioural reading instead.

contract.note: The behavioural reading (o3 can fail to track game state or apply the rules) is a fair, ordinary reading of 'vulnerable to the same overall issue'. Proving the stronger internal claim, that o3 has no world model, would need a different test. The window from o3's release to the post date is reasonable.

evidence.note: Acher's independent tests of o3 in May 2025 found clear illegal moves and a wrong reconstruction of the game state (the bxc3 case). He separates out the notation-only cases. This falls inside the target period.
The same report includes some legal and competent o3 games. This limits any reading that o3 always fails, but does not contradict vulnerability.

reviews.rationale: Under the behavioural reading, Acher's independent tests during the target period show o3 making substantive illegal moves and misrepresenting the game state. That meets the support condition. Some successful games show the failures are not universal but are consistent with 'vulnerable'. The tests use chess, not Marcus's tic-tac-toe variant, which fits 'same overall issue'.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own essay.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the subject (mechanistic interpretability), the target (world models in LLMs) and 'very limited success'. It is a retrospective observation.

contract.note: Reading the claim as 'recovery is narrow or incomplete, not zero' is a fair, ordinary reading of 'very limited success'. A stronger reading, that almost nothing has been recovered, would be harder to sustain given e2 and e3, so the interpretation matters.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed study of navigation models: the recovered maps are incoherent even where task performance is high. This is a substantive limit, although it does not survey the whole field.
Recovers chess-board state and changes later moves by intervening on it, a success beyond Othello. It is still a single constrained game in a small model trained only on chess games.
Finds linear space and time representations in Llama-2. The authors call these 'basic ingredients' of a world model, not a complete dynamic one.
A company disclosure about its own interpretability method: it captures only a fraction of the computation and is costly even on short prompts.

reviews.rationale: The literature through mid-2025 shows real but restricted recoveries: board state in chess and Othello, partial space and time features. It also shows coherence failures (e1) and admitted limits on large-model coverage (e4). Nothing shows systematic recovery of coherent, updatable world models across broad settings. This fits the contract's reading of 'very limited success'. e2 and e3 temper the essay's wider remark that Othello was the only solid result.
